title: Clocks and Calendars
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Clocks and Calendars. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Clock angles

The minute hand turns 6 degrees per minute; the hour hand turns 0.5 degrees per minute. At h hours and m minutes, their angular positions from 12 are (\(30h+0.5m\)) and (\(6m\)) degrees. The smaller angle is the lesser of their absolute difference and (\(360 ^\circ minus that difference\)).

Elapsed time

Convert times to minutes from a common reference or use 24-hour notation to cross noon and midnight safely. A 12-hour clock repeats its face, so attach AM/PM when the context requires it.

Calendar arithmetic

An ordinary year has 365 days, or 1 odd day beyond 52 weeks; a leap year has 366 days, or 2 odd days. In the Gregorian calendar, a year divisible by 4 is a leap year except century years, which must be divisible by 400.

Worked example: At 3:20, the minute hand is at (\(120 ^\circ\)) and the hour hand at (\(90+10=100 ^\circ\)). The smaller angle is 20 degrees.

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• For clock angles, include the hour hand's movement during the minutes elapsed.
  • Take the smaller of the two angles around the dial.
  • For weekdays, reduce elapsed days modulo 7.
  • Apply the century exception when checking leap years.
  • Convert a finish time after midnight to the next calendar day before subtracting.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• Minute hand speed is (\(6 ^\circ/\min\)); hour hand speed is (\(0.5 ^\circ/\min\)).
  • Relative hand speed is (\(5.5 ^\circ/\min\)).
  • Gregorian leap year: divisible by 4, except century years unless divisible by 400.
  • A date shifted by seven days falls on the same weekday.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    What is the smaller angle between the clock hands at 3:00?

    1. (\(60^\circ\))
    2. (\(90^\circ\))
    3. (\(120^\circ\))
    4. (\(180^\circ\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(90^\circ\))

    At 3:00, the hour hand is (\(90^\circ\)) from 12 and the minute hand is at (\(0^\circ\)). Their smaller angle is (\(90^\circ\)).

  2. Core:

    What day is 45 days after Sunday?

    1. Monday
    2. Tuesday
    3. Wednesday
    4. Thursday
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: Wednesday

    (\(45=6\cdot7+3\)), so move forward 3 days from Sunday: Wednesday.

  3. Foundation:

    How many odd days are in an ordinary 365-day year?

    1. (\(0\))
    2. (\(1\))
    3. (\(2\))
    4. (\(5\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(1\))

    There are 52 complete weeks and 1 extra day, so one odd day.

  4. Standard:

    Find the smaller angle between the clock hands at 2:30.

    1. (\(75 ^\circ\))
    2. (\(90 ^\circ\))
    3. (\(105 ^\circ\))
    4. (\(120 ^\circ\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(105 ^\circ\))

    Minute hand is at 180 degrees; hour hand is at (\(60+15=75\)) degrees. The difference is 105 degrees.

  5. Challenge:

    Is the year 2100 a leap year in the Gregorian calendar?

    1. Yes, because it is divisible by 4
    2. No, because it is a century not divisible by 400
    3. Yes, because all century years are leap years
    4. No, because it is not divisible by 4
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: No, because it is a century not divisible by 400

    Century years must be divisible by 400. Since 2100 is divisible by 100 but not 400, it is not a leap year.
